pathway.title: ACCO BRANDS Corp — Full credit assessment
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: - Earnings, not liquidity, are the weak point. Derived EBITDA fell 17.98% in FY2025 against a net sales fall of 8.49%, a ratio of 2.12x, because the cost base is largely fixed, and the 2026 recovery in reported operating income comes from USD 15.1 million of net tariff refunds that may not recur: without them third-quarter operating income is USD 15.2 million against USD 26.0 million a year earlier, and gross margin in the same quarter is 30.42% against 32.99%. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_acco_acco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 41; 10-K_2025-12-31_acco_acco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 62; 10-Q_2026-09-30_acco_acco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 29; 10-Q_2026-09-30_acco_acco-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 30–31; calculation C06; calculation C10; calculation C11

- Leverage is high on the derived measure and cannot be reconciled to the issuer's own covenant ratio. Derived net debt is 4.49x EBITDA, 4.88x pro forma for the Trust acquisition of 2026-10-01 and 4.46x pro forma for the October 2026 tariff refunds, against a reported covenant ratio of 3.60x and a maximum of 4.25x. The maximum falls to 4.00x for the third and fourth quarters of 2027, which would cut the reported gap from 0.65x to 0.40x if the ratio did not move; the EBITDA cushion cannot be calculated because the covenant definitions are not supplied. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_acco_acco-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 10–11; 10-Q_2026-09-30_acco_acco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 34; calculation C02; calculation C15

- Liquidity buys time, but almost all principal falls due in one window. Liquidity is USD 428.4 million against a mid-year trough of USD 311.2 million, no final maturity falls before March 2029, and 99.17% of principal is due in 2029, with the credit agreement requiring the 4.25% notes to be refinanced by September 2028. Refinancing the USD 575.0 million at the 5.49% weighted rate now paid on the secured facilities would add USD 7.13 million a year and lower derived interest cover from 3.63x to 3.11x; market access is not established because no rating or price is supplied. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_acco_acco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-Q_2026-09-30_acco_acco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_acco_acco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 34; 10-Q_2026-09-30_acco_acco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 35; calculation C01; calculation C13; calculation C14

- Customer concentration and private-label competition limit pricing power. The five largest customers are 31.79% of FY2025 net sales and their receivables are 32.53% of year-end receivables, while price increases net of programs offset only 18.89% of the volume lost in the nine months to 2026-09-30. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_acco_acco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-K_2025-12-31_acco_acco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-K_2025-12-31_acco_acco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 62; 10-K_2025-12-31_acco_acco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 106; 10-Q_2026-09-30_acco_acco-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 33–34; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C05; calculation C09

- Cost and capital flexibility is real but partly used. USD 90.0 million of the USD 100.0 million annualized savings target is realized, capital expenditure is 1.17% of net sales, and the 2026 payout cap of USD 40.0 million bounds shareholder leakage; the remaining USD 10.0 million of savings and USD 27.0 million of annual dividends are the levers left. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_acco_acco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 63; 10-Q_2026-09-30_acco_acco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_acco_acco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 36; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C05; calculation C18

- Governance and financial policy add little independent risk. No sponsor or controlling holder is identified, FY2025 payouts of USD 42.1 million were 82.9% of free cash flow, and the payout cap and USD 35.0 million term loan prepayment in the 2025 amendment show lenders obtained restraint in return for covenant relief. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_acco_acco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 39; 10-K_2025-12-31_acco_acco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 63; 10-K_2025-12-31_acco_acco-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 75–76; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C05

cells.text: Branded consumer, technology and business products sold to schools, homes and workplaces through retailers, e-commerce, dealers and wholesalers; about 75% of FY2025 net sales came from brands ranked first or second in their categories, which is a management statement
Brand position supports shelf space and pricing, but demand is discretionary and the ranking is management language
Americas net sales 894.4, or 58.7% of 1,524.7; International 630.3, or 41.3%; the issuer prints 59% and 41%
Two regions spread demand; International carries euro and Australian dollar exposure

Comparable net sales changed -8.0% in FY2024, -9.3% in FY2025 and -3.7% in the nine months to 2026-09-30; reported nine-month sales rose 3.9% with EPOS and currency; the issuer cites technology peripherals as the 2026 decline
Falling organic volume is the main operating risk

Five largest customers 484.7 of 1,524.7, or 31.79%; Amazon 158.1, or about 10%; five-customer share 31.98% in FY2024 and 33.23% in FY2023; top five trade receivables 117.0 of 359.7, or 32.53%; third-quarter 2026 reserve for a customer liquidation 4.8
A loss or insolvency at a top customer hits volume and receivables together

About 40% of products made in own plants and 60% sourced from lower-cost countries, mainly Asia; tariff refunds of 21.3 received in the third quarter of 2026; new Section 301 tariffs effective 2026-07-24
Tariff changes move gross margin and working capital; refunds are one-off gains

Annualized savings target of about 100.0 by the end of 2026, about 90.0 realized since inception and about 30.0 in nine months 2026; restructuring cost 21.6 in FY2025 and 8.3 in nine months 2026; 17.4 restructuring liability at 2026-09-30
Savings offset volume declines (90% of target realized), but severance cash competes with debt service
Gross margin 32.8% in FY2025 and 33.1% in nine months 2026; operating margin 6.1% in FY2025 and 4.4% in nine months 2026
Margins have held despite lower volume, helped in 2026 by tariff refunds

Sales lowest in the first quarter; back-to-school lifts the second and third quarters; operating cash flow arrives in the second half; revolver availability 204.8 at 2026-06-30 and 253.7 at 2026-09-30; total available liquidity 428.4 (cash 174.7 plus availability) at 2026-09-30
Revolver use peaks mid-year, so the quarterly path matters more than year-end
Capital expenditure 17.9 in FY2025, or 1.17% of net sales; depreciation 26.6
Low capital needs leave cash for debt service while footprint rationalization continues
EPOS acquired 2026-01-30 and Trust 2026-10-01; gaming accessories depend on licences from the three major console makers and on platform certifications for audio products
Growth strategy adds integration and licence-dependence risk

runs.text: - Liquidity and the maturity profile give the issuer time. Liquidity is USD 428.4 million, the mid-year trough was USD 311.2 million and no final maturity falls before March 2029, so debt service does not depend on new market access for about two years. Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_acco_acco-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 32; 10-Q_2026-09-30_acco_acco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 34; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C01

- The cost programme and low capital needs protect cash. About USD 90.0 million of savings is realized and capital expenditure is 1.17% of net sales, which keeps free cash flow positive when sales fall. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_acco_acco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 63; 10-Q_2026-09-30_acco_acco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 36; calculation C05

- No sponsor and a capped payout limit leakage. Payouts were 82.9% of FY2025 free cash flow and the 2026 cap is USD 40.0 million, so cash is more likely to stay in the company than in a sponsor-owned peer. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_acco_acco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 63; 10-K_2025-12-31_acco_acco-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 75–76; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C05

- The fixed 4.25% coupon holds interest cost down until 2029. It applies to 65.25% of principal, so cash interest of USD 43.2 million is covered 3.63x despite lower earnings. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_acco_acco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-Q_2026-09-30_acco_acco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 35; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C14

- Earnings fall faster than sales. Derived EBITDA fell 17.98% on a net sales fall of 8.49%, and without USD 15.1 million of net tariff refunds third-quarter operating income was USD 15.2 million against USD 26.0 million, so deleveraging through earnings is not in evidence. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_acco_acco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 41; 10-K_2025-12-31_acco_acco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 62; 10-Q_2026-09-30_acco_acco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 29; calculation C06; calculation C11

- Leverage is high and its covenant measure cannot be reproduced. Derived net debt is 4.49x EBITDA and 4.88x pro forma for the Trust acquisition, against a reported ratio of 3.60x, and the maximum steps down to 4.00x in the second half of 2027. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_acco_acco-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 10–11; 10-Q_2026-09-30_acco_acco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 34; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C02; calculation C15

- Almost all debt is due in 2029. 99.17% of principal falls due in 2029 and the notes must be refinanced by September 2028, when a coupon at the 5.49% secured rate would lower derived cover to 3.11x. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_acco_acco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-Q_2026-09-30_acco_acco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_acco_acco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 35; calculation C13; calculation C14

- Customers and competition limit pricing. The five largest customers are 31.79% of net sales with 32.53% of receivables, and price offset only 18.89% of volume loss. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_acco_acco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-K_2025-12-31_acco_acco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 62; 10-K_2025-12-31_acco_acco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 106; 10-Q_2026-09-30_acco_acco-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 33–34; calculation C05; calculation C09

cells.text: ACCO Brands Corporation, a Delaware corporation; common stock listed on the New York Stock Exchange as ACCO; accelerated filer
The issuer is the listed parent, so the public shareholder base and not a sponsor sits above the debt
Leased headquarters in Lake Zurich, Illinois; manufacturing in the U.S., Europe, Brazil, Mexico and Australia; distribution centres in regional markets
Operations in several currencies and tariff regimes
About 4,700 full-time and part-time employees, about 3,600 outside the U.S.; about 200 U.S. manufacturing and distribution employees under collective bargaining; no strikes in five years
Mostly non-U.S. and mostly non-union, which limits labour-cost rigidity in the U.S.
Top 12 brands about 1.1 billion of FY2025 net sales; brands include At-A-Glance, Kensington, Leitz, Mead, PowerA and Swingline
A concentrated brand set drives most revenue
United States 647.3, or 42.5%, and outside the United States 877.4, or 57.5%, of 1,524.7
Majority of revenue is in non-U.S. currencies
90,170,277 shares outstanding at 2026-03-02 and 92,341,513 at 2026-10-23; about 6,666 record holders at 2026-03-02; market value held by non-affiliates about 316.1 at 2025-06-30
Equity value is small relative to debt, so equity is a thin cushion
Not supplied: no controlling shareholder, sponsor or director holdings are stated in the supplied filings; the proxy statement that would hold them was not supplied
No sponsor extraction or support can be assessed from this evidence
President and chief executive officer in role since 2023 and chief financial officer since 2022; the general counsel joined in 2025 and the president of International took the role in 2026
Finance leadership has been in place since before the 2025 amendment; two other senior roles changed in 2025 and 2026
KPMG LLP, auditor since 2009; unqualified-style opinions on the 2024 and 2025 statements and on internal control over financial reporting at 2025-12-31; disclosure controls effective at 2026-09-30
Reporting quality is not a flagged concern
Bank of America, N.A. is administrative agent under the Third Amended and Restated Credit Agreement dated 2017-01-27
Lender group and agent are named, but lender identities and holdings are not

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: No new debt was issued in the periods the filings cover and no refinancing is pending; the financing event that matters is the July 2025 covenant amendment, which bought covenant room at the price of a USD 35.0 million term loan prepayment and a cap on 2026 payouts, so the risk is headroom rather than new secured debt ranking ahead of existing creditors. The amendment raised the maximum leverage ratio to 4.50x for the third and fourth quarters of 2025, 4.75x for the first and second quarters of 2026 and 4.25x for the third and fourth quarters of 2026, with the original 4.50x and 4.00x levels returning afterwards, and it changed lien, debt and restricted-payment baskets through 2026-12-31. The reported ratio was 4.13x against a 4.50x maximum at 2025-12-31 and 3.60x against 4.25x at 2026-09-30. The secured credit agreement, reduced in October 2024 to a EUR 184.8 million term loan facility and a USD 467.5 million revolver, falls due on 2029-10-30, with a requirement to refinance the USD 575.0 million of 4.25% senior unsecured notes due March 2029 by September 2028. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_acco_acco-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 75–76; 10-Q_2026-09-30_acco_acco-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 10–11; 10-Q_2026-09-30_acco_acco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 34; 10-K_2024-12-31_acco_acco-20241231.htm.jsonl, page 73; 10-K_2025-12-31_acco_acco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 77

Acquisitions are small and cash-settled. Buro in Australia and New Zealand closed on 2025-02-28 for USD 10.1 million, EPOS on 2026-01-30 for EUR 6.5 million at closing plus up to EUR 3.0 million of contingent consideration, and Trust on 2026-10-01 for about USD 57 million plus USD 5 million of preliminary adjustments, the last after the latest balance sheet and with no financing, cash acquired or earnings contribution disclosed, so its effect on leverage is not established. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_acco_acco-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 73–74; 10-Q_2026-09-30_acco_acco-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 7–9

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Two limits matter to creditors. The reported Consolidated Leverage Ratio of 3.60x against a 4.25x maximum cannot be reproduced, because no filing reports EBITDA or the covenant definition, and the Trust acquisition completed on 2026-10-01 falls after the latest balance sheet with its funding not stated, so period-end borrowings may not describe the position at the as-of date.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: All amounts are USD millions as printed in the filings and are exact at source precision. Ratios are differences between two ratios the issuer reports, not new measures.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Material: None of the five filings reports EBITDA, adjusted EBITDA, covenant EBITDA or free cash flow, so the reported Consolidated Leverage Ratio of 3.60x against a 4.25x maximum cannot be reproduced. Any EBITDA-based leverage in later work has to be a labelled derivation from operating income plus depreciation and amortization, with the bargain purchase gain and tariff refunds treated explicitly, and it will not equal the covenant measure.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Material: The Trust acquisition completed on 2026-10-01 falls after the 2026-09-30 balance sheet. The quarterly report gives an unadjusted purchase price of about USD 57 million plus preliminary adjustments of USD 5 million, but no funding source, no later borrowing and no pro forma debt or leverage. Borrowings and leverage at the as-of date are therefore not established, and the September position may understate them.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Minor: The Interest Coverage Ratio, with a minimum of 3.00x, is reported only at year-end 2024 and year-end 2025. None of the 2026 quarterly reports states the test or a reading, so headroom on this covenant is not established for 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Minor: No filing states whether cash is restricted, trapped or held outside the United States, so the USD 174.7 million of cash and cash equivalents is not confirmed as unrestricted. Liquidity of USD 428.4 million counts all of it, and the filings do not say whether any covenant limits drawing on the revolver.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Minor: The latest by-year debt table is at 2025-12-31 and none is printed at 2026-09-30. The Q3 report says there are no debt maturities before March 2029 while USD 41.3 million of debt is classed as current. At year-end 2025 the current USD 30.8 million was term loan amortization of USD 7.2 million plus U.S. dollar revolver borrowings of USD 23.6 million, so the two statements differ in wording, not in amount.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Minor: The security and borrower of USD 7.3 million of other borrowings are not printed. The debt table lists them after the unsecured notes, yet the issuer's USD 306.2 million total for senior secured facility debt equals the four secured lines plus these borrowings.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Minor: Directors, committee structure, compensation and share ownership sit in the proxy statement that the 2025 annual report incorporates by reference, and it was not supplied; only the executive officers and the annual report's own statements on governance are available.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Scope limit, not counted: The run settings declare no legal documents, and none were supplied. Covenant levels, the Consolidated Leverage Ratio definition, baskets, the requirement to refinance the unsecured notes by September 2028 and guarantee and lien terms are known only from the summaries in the filings, so covenant capacity, legal priority and recovery work cannot be completed; the credit agreement, its eight amendments and the indenture are listed as exhibits incorporated by reference.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Scope limit, not counted: Guarantor-level financial information is not supplied. The unsecured notes are guaranteed by existing and future U.S. subsidiaries other than certain excluded subsidiaries, so the share of earnings and assets outside the guarantor group cannot be measured and structural subordination cannot be sized.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Scope limit, not counted: No credit rating, market quote, deal term, peer set, portfolio limit, earnings release or lender presentation was supplied, and the run settings leave these inputs blank rather than zero. Ratings, market-implied and relative-value work cannot be done on this evidence.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Scope limit, not counted: Unconditional purchase commitments of USD 116.9 million are reported only at year-end 2025, and no filing mentions factoring, supplier finance or securitization, so none is assumed; the 2026 reports do not update the commitment figure.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leverage on carrying-value debt and derived EBITDA was 5.07x at FY2025 and is 5.60x on a last-twelve-months basis at 2026-09-30, because carrying debt rose from USD 836.8 million to USD 878.1 million while derived EBITDA fell from USD 165.1 million to USD 156.7 million. The FY2024 ratio of 23.12x is not a trend point: it is struck after a non-cash impairment of USD 165.2 million, and before it the same ratio is 4.15x. The issuer's covenant ratio of 3.60x against a 4.25x maximum is 2.00x below the derived figure, and without the covenant EBITDA the difference cannot be bridged, so the covenant figure is quoted but not used as a leverage measure here.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Debt service is covered but cover has slipped: derived EBITDA covers cash interest 3.63x over the last twelve months against 3.81x in FY2025, with cash interest paid at USD 43.2 million. Operating cash flow of USD 99.6 million in the nine months to 2026-09-30 compares with USD 38.1 million a year earlier, but the issuer's own split shows cash earnings before working capital of USD 75.2 million against USD 78.4 million and a smaller outflow through other assets and liabilities of USD 32.9 million against USD 88.7 million, so the gain comes from lower payments such as cash taxes of USD 10.1 million against USD 25.4 million, not from higher earnings. Free cash flow after capital expenditure is USD 114.0 million over the last twelve months, before dividends of USD 20.8 million in the nine months.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity is USD 428.4 million: USD 174.7 million of cash and USD 253.7 million available on the USD 467.5 million revolving facility after USD 7.5 million of letters of credit. That is up from USD 311.2 million at 2026-06-30, the lowest of the readings supplied, and the filings place the first final maturity in March 2029, so refinancing risk is a 2028 and 2029 question rather than a near-term one. Cash is netted in full in net debt although no filing says whether any of it is restricted, so the reported net debt is the most favourable reading.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against reading leverage as high is the issuer's own covenant ratio of 3.60x, which stays inside the 4.25x maximum, together with the rebuilt liquidity and the seasonal pattern that makes September cash flow stronger than the first half. It would win if the covenant EBITDA reconciliation showed add-backs that bridge the 2.00x difference to the derived ratio, or if fourth-quarter cash flow repaid revolver drawings. It would lose if the Trust acquisition was debt funded and earnings stayed at the 2026 level.

A further USD 5.0 million of tariff refunds received in October 2026 would lower net leverage to 4.46x. These are separate standalone adjustments to the 2026-09-30 position, not a forecast of year-end net debt.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - High: No filing reports EBITDA, adjusted EBITDA, covenant EBITDA or free cash flow, so reported EBITDA is derived from operating income, depreciation and amortization, and the issuer's covenant ratio of 3.60x cannot be reproduced; the derived ratio is 2.00x higher. This restricts every leverage and coverage conclusion to a labelled derivation and blocks covenant-headroom work. The covenant EBITDA reconciliation and the credit agreement definitions would close it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - High: The Trust acquisition completed on 2026-10-01 falls after the latest balance sheet, and the quarterly report states no funding source, cash acquired, subsequent borrowing or pro forma debt. The post-balance-sheet net debt of about USD 62 million is a standalone approximation that excludes Trust's earnings. The next quarterly report or a financing announcement would close it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Medium: No by-year maturity table is printed at 2026-09-30, so the maturity chart and the principal reconciliation use the table at 2025-12-31, and its 2026 amount includes revolver borrowings classed as current. The quarterly report's statement that no debt matures before March 2029 refers to final maturities, while USD 41.3 million is classed as current. A by-year table at the latest date would close this.

fields.value: - Medium: The minimum Interest Coverage Ratio of 3.00x is reported only at year-end 2024 and year-end 2025, and none of the 2026 quarterly reports states the test or a reading. Headroom on that covenant is not established for 2026; the compliance certificate would close it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Medium: No filing states whether cash is restricted, trapped or held outside the United States, so all cash is netted in net debt and in liquidity of USD 428.4 million. A note on cash restrictions would close it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Medium: Revolver availability at 2023-12-31 is not printed in the supplied reports, so the FY2023 liquidity row has no undrawn figure; the 2023 annual report would close it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Medium: The executed credit agreement is not supplied, so the shared rank of the four secured facility lines, the borrowers by facility and the terms of the requirement to refinance the unsecured notes by September 2028 rest on summaries. This restricts the debt stack and any priority conclusion; the agreement would close it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Low: Source dashes are kept as missing, not zero: gain on disposal of assets in FY2023, FY2024 and 2026, impairment in FY2025, notes payable at 2025-12-31, and several cash flow lines. Reported totals reconcile, but component sums cannot certify each dash as zero; a note stating nil would close them.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Low: Instrument-level carrying values are not disclosed, only principal by instrument and one aggregate of USD 3.1 million of unamortized issuance costs, so the debt table shows principal and a financing cost adjustment. The security, rank and borrower of USD 7.3 million of other borrowings are not stated, so they stay out of the debt stack.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Low: Quarterly cash flows are printed year to date only, so a discrete third-quarter cash flow needs differencing; the H1 2026 and Q1 2026 columns appear only in the balance sheet. Capital expenditure is not split between maintenance and growth, and standardized funds from operations is not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Low: Cash additions to property, plant and equipment differ from the capital spend printed in the segment note (USD 17.9 million against USD 19.5 million in FY2025), and the filings do not explain the difference; cash additions are used.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Low: The issuer states no adjusted EBITDA and no add-backs, so the adjusted ratios and the EBITDA bridge are not written; net tariff refunds of USD 15.1 million in the third quarter of 2026 are inside reported EBITDA and their recurrence is not stated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Business and governance fact pack for ACCO BRANDS Corp (issuer acco-712034) as of 2026-11-18 under the credit snapshot pathway. Scope is the business and operating model, ownership and control, governance and capital-allocation behaviour, transactions and dated events, taken from the five supplied filings.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: ACCO is a publicly listed branded-products business whose credit risk comes from shrinking demand, tariff exposure and customer concentration rather than sponsor behaviour, but the 2025 covenant amendment shows the limits of its cushion. No sponsor or controlling holder is identified in the supplied filings, and shareholder payouts of USD 42.1 million in FY2025 were below free cash flow of USD 50.8 million.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_acco_acco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 38; 10-K_2025-12-31_acco_acco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 39; 10-K_2025-12-31_acco_acco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 63; 10-K_2025-12-31_acco_acco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 75; calculation C06

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The governance risk level is Medium on evidence that is incomplete rather than adverse: the proxy statement that holds director, pay and ownership detail was not supplied, and the credit agreement that sets payout capacity is summarised only in the filings.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Demand, not governance, is the main operating risk. Comparable net sales fell 9.3% in FY2025 after a fall of 8.0% in FY2024 and fell 3.7% in the nine months to 2026-09-30; the issuer attributes FY2025 volume losses to lower consumer and business demand and tariff disruption, and 2026 declines to technology peripherals. Reported sales rose 3.9% in 2026 only because EPOS and currency added to them. Falling volume reaches creditors through lower earnings on a largely fixed cost base, which the cost programme has so far offset: the issuer states about USD 90.0 million of annualized savings realized against a target of about USD 100.0 million by the end of 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Customer concentration is material. The five largest customers took USD 484.7 million, or 31.79% of FY2025 net sales, and the largest, Amazon, took USD 158.1 million, or about 10%; their receivables were USD 117.0 million, or 32.53% of year-end accounts receivable. Management itself says the largest customers have significant negotiating leverage and that concentration raises customer credit risk, and a reserve of USD 4.8 million for a customer liquidation was booked in the third quarter of 2026, which shows the receivable exposure is real.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_acco_acco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-K_2025-12-31_acco_acco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 62; 10-K_2025-12-31_acco_acco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 106; 10-Q_2026-09-30_acco_acco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 31; calculation C01; calculation C09

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Strategy is moving toward technology peripherals through small, cheap acquisitions, and the funding of the latest is not stated. EPOS was bought on 2026-01-30 for a net USD 1.1 million after cash acquired and produced a bargain purchase gain of USD 33.8 million because it was losing money, so integration and restructuring cash, not the price, is the cost. The Trust acquisition completed on 2026-10-01 at an unadjusted price of about USD 57 million plus USD 5 million of adjustments, after the latest balance sheet, with no financing disclosed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Payout policy is mixed rather than extractive. The quarterly dividend per share has been unchanged for three years and cost USD 27.0 million in FY2025; with USD 15.1 million of buybacks, nearly all in the first quarter of 2025, that was 82.9% of free cash flow. After the July 2025 covenant amendment, 2026 dividends plus buybacks are capped at the greater of USD 40.0 million or 1% of consolidated total assets, which is the USD 40.0 million figure at the 2025 year-end balance sheet; no shares were repurchased in the nine months to 2026-09-30, when dividends took 23.4% of free cash flow and 52.0% of the cap. The filings do not say whether the wider standing baskets, which allow a further USD 75.0 million a year at 0.25x inside the covenant and unlimited payments at 3.25x or lower, apply again after 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Seasonality moves the revolver through the year. Sales are lowest in the first quarter, back-to-school lifts the second and third quarters, and operating cash flow arrives in the second half, so revolver availability fell to USD 204.8 million at 2026-06-30 before recovering to USD 253.7 million at 2026-09-30. The quarterly path, not the year-end snapshot, is what to monitor.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Exposure outside the United States is 57.5% of net sales and sits in euro, Australian dollar and other currencies, matched in part by euro and Australian dollar borrowings; about 40% of products are made in the issuer's own plants and 60% are sourced, mainly from Asia, so tariff and currency changes reach gross margin directly. Net tariff refunds added USD 15.1 million to third-quarter 2026 operating income and may not recur.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against a cautious reading is financial: the issuer reports a covenant leverage ratio of 3.60x against a 4.25x maximum, liquidity has rebuilt to USD 428.4 million, capital expenditure is only about 1.17% of net sales, no payout exceeds free cash flow, and about USD 90.0 million of cost savings are already realized. The Medium level would move down to Low if the proxy statement showed independent control and no related-party payments and if the Trust purchase proved to be funded from cash on hand; it would move up to High if payouts after 2026 drew on the wider baskets while leverage stayed above 3.25x, if a top customer was lost, or if fourth-quarter cash flow failed to repay the revolver drawings that peaked in mid-year.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: No new debt was issued in the periods the filings cover and no refinancing is pending; the financing event that matters is the July 2025 covenant amendment, which bought covenant room at the price of a USD 35.0 million term loan prepayment and a cap on 2026 payouts, so the risk is headroom rather than new secured debt ranking ahead of existing creditors. The amendment raised the maximum leverage ratio to 4.50x for the third and fourth quarters of 2025, 4.75x for the first and second quarters of 2026 and 4.25x for the third and fourth quarters of 2026, with the original 4.50x and 4.00x levels returning afterwards, and it changed lien, debt and restricted-payment baskets through 2026-12-31. The reported ratio was 4.13x against a 4.50x maximum at 2025-12-31 and 3.60x against 4.25x at 2026-09-30. The secured credit agreement, reduced in October 2024 to a EUR 184.8 million term loan facility and a USD 467.5 million revolver, falls due on 2029-10-30, with a requirement to refinance the USD 575.0 million of 4.25% senior unsecured notes due March 2029 by September 2028.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fundamental credit synthesis for ACCO BRANDS Corp (issuer acco-712034) as of 2026-11-18 under the credit snapshot pathway. Scope is the integrated view of business quality, financial profile, outlook, downside and monitoring, built on the five supplied filings and the three earlier analyses.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: ACCO is an adequate but constrained credit: a mature brand business with falling volume has the liquidity and cost savings to reach its 2029 maturities, but its earnings absorb volume losses badly and its leverage leaves little room for a costly refinancing. Derived net debt is USD 703.4 million, or 4.49x last-twelve-months EBITDA, and USD 765.4 million, or 4.88x, pro forma for the Trust acquisition of 2026-10-01, while the October 2026 tariff refunds alone would lower it to USD 698.4 million, or 4.46x; total liquidity is USD 428.4 million.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_acco_acco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 34; calculation C01; calculation C02; calculation C03

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The main downside path is volume loss on a fixed cost base, which cut derived EBITDA by 17.98% on a net sales fall of 8.49% in FY2025, and it leaves the 2028 refinancing of the USD 575.0 million 4.25% notes as the first hard test of that weaker earnings base.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_acco_acco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 41; 10-K_2025-12-31_acco_acco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 62; calculation C06; calculation C13

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Earnings, not liquidity, are the weak point. Derived EBITDA fell 17.98% in FY2025 against a net sales fall of 8.49%, a ratio of 2.12x, because the cost base is largely fixed, and the 2026 recovery in reported operating income comes from USD 15.1 million of net tariff refunds that may not recur: without them third-quarter operating income is USD 15.2 million against USD 26.0 million a year earlier, and gross margin in the same quarter is 30.42% against 32.99%.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_acco_acco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 41; 10-K_2025-12-31_acco_acco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 62; 10-Q_2026-09-30_acco_acco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 29; 10-Q_2026-09-30_acco_acco-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 30–31; calculation C06; calculation C10; calculation C11

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Leverage is high on the derived measure and cannot be reconciled to the issuer's own covenant ratio. Derived net debt is 4.49x EBITDA, 4.88x pro forma for the Trust acquisition of 2026-10-01 and 4.46x pro forma for the October 2026 tariff refunds, against a reported covenant ratio of 3.60x and a maximum of 4.25x. The maximum falls to 4.00x for the third and fourth quarters of 2027, which would cut the reported gap from 0.65x to 0.40x if the ratio did not move; the EBITDA cushion cannot be calculated because the covenant definitions are not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_acco_acco-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 10–11; 10-Q_2026-09-30_acco_acco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 34; calculation C02; calculation C15

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Liquidity buys time, but almost all principal falls due in one window. Liquidity is USD 428.4 million against a mid-year trough of USD 311.2 million, no final maturity falls before March 2029, and 99.17% of principal is due in 2029, with the credit agreement requiring the 4.25% notes to be refinanced by September 2028. Refinancing the USD 575.0 million at the 5.49% weighted rate now paid on the secured facilities would add USD 7.13 million a year and lower derived interest cover from 3.63x to 3.11x; market access is not established because no rating or price is supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_acco_acco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-Q_2026-09-30_acco_acco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_acco_acco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 34; 10-Q_2026-09-30_acco_acco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 35; calculation C01; calculation C13; calculation C14

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Customer concentration and private-label competition limit pricing power. The five largest customers are 31.79% of FY2025 net sales and their receivables are 32.53% of year-end receivables, while price increases net of programs offset only 18.89% of the volume lost in the nine months to 2026-09-30.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_acco_acco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-K_2025-12-31_acco_acco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-K_2025-12-31_acco_acco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 62; 10-K_2025-12-31_acco_acco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 106; 10-Q_2026-09-30_acco_acco-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 33–34; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C05; calculation C09

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Cost and capital flexibility is real but partly used. USD 90.0 million of the USD 100.0 million annualized savings target is realized, capital expenditure is 1.17% of net sales, and the 2026 payout cap of USD 40.0 million bounds shareholder leakage; the remaining USD 10.0 million of savings and USD 27.0 million of annual dividends are the levers left.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_acco_acco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 63; 10-Q_2026-09-30_acco_acco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_acco_acco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 36; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C05; calculation C18

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Governance and financial policy add little independent risk. No sponsor or controlling holder is identified, FY2025 payouts of USD 42.1 million were 82.9% of free cash flow, and the payout cap and USD 35.0 million term loan prepayment in the 2025 amendment show lenders obtained restraint in return for covenant relief.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_acco_acco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 39; 10-K_2025-12-31_acco_acco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 63; 10-K_2025-12-31_acco_acco-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 75–76; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C05

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence for a more favourable reading is the issuer's own covenant ratio of 3.60x against a 4.25x maximum, liquidity of USD 428.4 million, free cash flow of USD 114.0 million over the last twelve months and USD 90.0 million of realized savings; on that evidence the credit is a stable, slowly deleveraging company. That evidence is weaker than it looks, because the free cash flow owes much to lower cash tax and other payments and the covenant ratio rests on a definition the filings do not give. The view would improve if the covenant reconciliation showed add-backs that bridge the 2.00x gap to the derived ratio, if fourth-quarter cash flow cut revolver borrowings from USD 206.3 million and the Trust purchase was funded from cash on hand, or if comparable sales stabilised. It would weaken if comparable sales fell by more than the 9.3% of FY2025, if the net tariff refunds proved to be the only reason operating income rose, or if the notes could not be refinanced near the 5.49% paid on the secured facilities.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_acco_acco-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 10–11; 10-Q_2026-09-30_acco_acco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 34; 10-Q_2026-09-30_acco_acco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 35; 10-K_2025-12-31_acco_acco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 41; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C01; calculation C02; calculation C04; calculation C13

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No agency rating, bond price or loan price is supplied, so the judgement on refinancing capacity rests on leverage, liquidity and the maturity profile alone; a market read could move that judgement either way and is the main reason the refinancing view is stated as dependent rather than assessed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Derived EBITDA carries no covenant add-backs, so every leverage figure here is on the derived basis and is 2.00x above the issuer's reported ratio; the downside conclusion therefore shows direction and size on that basis and does not establish when a covenant would bind.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The operating-leverage ratio of 2.12x rests on two annual points, FY2024 after adding back a non-cash impairment and FY2025, so it indicates the order of magnitude of earnings sensitivity and not a stable coefficient; the illustrative leverage of 5.47x after a repeat of that earnings decline inherits the same limit.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_acco_acco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 62; 10-K_2025-12-31_acco_acco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 41; calculation C06; calculation C19

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The earnings contribution and funding of the Trust acquisition are not stated, so its effect on the 2027 outlook is not established and the pro forma leverage of 4.88x is a standalone adjustment to the 2026-09-30 position.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: ACCO sells branded consumer, technology and business products to schools, homes and workplaces through retailers, e-commerce and dealers, and about 75% of FY2025 net sales came from brands the issuer ranks first or second in their categories; that supports shelf space, but it is the issuer's own ranking and demand follows school, office and consumer spending, which has fallen in each period since the start of 2024. The Americas supplied 58.7% and International 41.3% of FY2025 net sales, and 57.5% of sales were outside the United States, so the business carries euro, Australian dollar and tariff exposure that a domestic peer would not.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_acco_acco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-K_2025-12-31_acco_acco-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 103–104; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C05

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash generation is seasonal, which matters for debt service and liquidity preservation: operating cash flow arrives in the second half, so revolver availability fell to USD 204.8 million at 2026-06-30 before recovering to USD 253.7 million at 2026-09-30, and net debt moved from USD 824.0 million to USD 703.4 million in the same quarter. Cash-flow visibility is therefore good within a year and weak across years, because there are no long-term contracts that fix volume.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_acco_acco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-Q_2026-06-30_acco_acco-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 32; 10-Q_2026-09-30_acco_acco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 34; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C01; calculation C17

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The issuer is a publicly listed parent with no sponsor, parent or controlling holder identified in the supplied filings, so there is neither sponsor extraction risk nor sponsor support, and the equity cushion is thin: shares held by non-affiliates were worth about USD 316.1 million at 2025-06-30 against debt of USD 878.1 million at 2026-09-30. Financial policy is set by a board that kept the quarterly dividend unchanged through a covenant amendment year and paid out 82.9% of free cash flow in FY2025, which is moderate but not conservative; the 2026 payout cap is the binding constraint for creditors, and what applies after 2026 is not stated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_acco_acco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-K_2025-12-31_acco_acco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 39; 10-K_2025-12-31_acco_acco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 63; 10-K_2025-12-31_acco_acco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 76; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C01; calculation C05

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The USD 575.0 million of unsecured notes are guaranteed by existing and future U.S. subsidiaries, while the USD 306.2 million of credit agreement debt is guaranteed and secured by substantially all assets of the company and certain guarantor subsidiaries, so secured lenders rank ahead of noteholders in practice. With 57.5% of sales outside the United States, what share of earnings and assets sits inside the guarantor perimeter is not established, and that decides how much of the derived EBITDA noteholders can reach; the ranking and recovery work belongs to Structural priority.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_acco_acco-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 9–11; 10-Q_2026-09-30_acco_acco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 35; 10-K_2025-12-31_acco_acco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 103; calculation C01; calculation C05

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue is discretionary, concentrated and partly in structural decline. Comparable net sales fell 8.0% in FY2024, 9.3% in FY2025 and 3.7% in the nine months to 2026-09-30, and the 3.9% rise in reported nine-month sales came only from USD 56.4 million of EPOS sales and USD 27.6 million of currency. The issuer states that demand for paper-based products has declined as hybrid work and education spread and as the German government replaces paper-based processes, and that it expects the decline to continue; part of the volume loss is therefore not cyclical and will not return in an upturn. The stated growth strategy rests on technology peripherals, yet the issuer cites global declines in that category in 2026, so the offset to the paper-based decline is not yet visible in sales.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2024-12-31_acco_acco-20241231.htm.jsonl, page 40; 10-K_2025-12-31_acco_acco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-K_2025-12-31_acco_acco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 41; 10-K_2025-12-31_acco_acco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-Q_2026-09-30_acco_acco-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 30–31; calculation C04; calculation C05

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Pricing power is limited. Price increases net of programs were USD 9.5 million in the nine months to 2026-09-30 against volume losses of USD 50.3 million, an offset of 18.89%, and the issuer says it has historically been unable to raise prices fast enough to cover cost increases and that customers trade down to lower priced products. The five largest customers are 31.79% of net sales and some import their own private-label goods, so a pricing dispute or a lost listing would reach volume and receivables together; revenue visibility is low.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_acco_acco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-K_2025-12-31_acco_acco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-K_2025-12-31_acco_acco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 22; 10-K_2025-12-31_acco_acco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 106; 10-Q_2026-09-30_acco_acco-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 33–34; calculation C05; calculation C09

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Margins have been defended by cost actions but not held by them. Gross margin was 33.3% in FY2024, 32.8% in FY2025 and 33.1% in the nine months to 2026-09-30, but the last figure includes USD 20.1 million of tariff refunds; without them the nine-month margin is 31.31% against 32.48% a year earlier and the third-quarter margin is 30.42% against 32.99%, even though the temporary tariffs ended in February 2026. The derived EBITDA margin has moved from 12.08% in FY2024 to 10.83% in FY2025 and 9.99% over the last twelve months.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_acco_acco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 41; 10-K_2025-12-31_acco_acco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 62; 10-Q_2026-09-30_acco_acco-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 27–28; 10-Q_2026-09-30_acco_acco-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 30–31; calculation C07; calculation C10

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The cost base is largely fixed: selling, general and administrative expenses of USD 346.7 million are 22.74% of net sales, and with depreciation, amortization and rent they turn lower volume into larger profit declines, which is why derived EBITDA fell 17.98% on a net sales fall of 8.49% in FY2025. Operating leverage cuts both ways but, with comparable sales still falling, it is the main margin risk. The cost programme has delivered about USD 90.0 million of its USD 100.0 million target, so only about USD 10.0 million of savings remains to offset further declines.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_acco_acco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 41; 10-K_2025-12-31_acco_acco-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 45–46; 10-Q_2026-09-30_acco_acco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 36; calculation C04; calculation C06; calculation C18

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Capital intensity is low and free cash flow is positive in every year supplied but unstable. Capital expenditure was USD 17.9 million, 1.17% of FY2025 net sales, so there is little spending to cut in a downturn, and free cash flow has been 54.64% of derived EBITDA in FY2023, 65.72% in FY2024, 30.77% in FY2025 and 72.75% over the last twelve months. The FY2025 low reflects a USD 65.2 million net outflow through other assets and liabilities, including restructuring, taxes, interest, pensions and incentives, and the recovery to USD 114.0 million over the last twelve months comes from lower payments of that kind rather than higher earnings, so free cash flow is not a steady source for debt reduction.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_acco_acco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 47; 10-K_2025-12-31_acco_acco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 63; 10-Q_2026-09-30_acco_acco-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 36–37; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C04; calculation C08

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash uses ahead of debt reduction are modest but real: dividends of USD 27.0 million in FY2025, restructuring cash with a USD 14.8 million liability due within twelve months, lease liabilities of USD 71.2 million and pension and post-retirement obligations of USD 110.6 million that the issuer carries outside debt. The German pension plan alone was unfunded by USD 103.6 million at 2025-12-31, which makes it a debt-like claim that leverage on reported debt does not count.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_acco_acco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 63; 10-K_2025-12-31_acco_acco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 80; 10-Q_2026-09-30_acco_acco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_acco_acco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_acco_acco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 16; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C01; calculation C04

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Rivalry is intense and pricing is exposed: the issuer describes a highly competitive market with low barriers to entry for certain products, private-label suppliers and customers importing their own goods, so price competition rises in weak periods, and with price offsetting only 18.89% of volume loss the issuer has not been able to hold margin by pricing. Substitutes are the structural threat: digital tools replace paper-based products and demand for them is expected to keep declining, which caps the earnings that mature categories can contribute to debt service.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_acco_acco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-K_2025-12-31_acco_acco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-Q_2026-09-30_acco_acco-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 33–34; calculation C09

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Buyer power is high: the five largest customers are 31.79% of net sales, large customers demand lower prices and shorter lead times, and management says concentration increases customer credit risk. Supplier power is moderate but tariff-linked: a majority of products are bought from lower-cost countries, mainly in Asia, in U.S. dollars, and gaming accessories depend on licences from three major console makers, so a tariff change or a licence loss reaches gross margin directly and cannot be passed on quickly.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_acco_acco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-K_2025-12-31_acco_acco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-K_2025-12-31_acco_acco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-K_2025-12-31_acco_acco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-K_2025-12-31_acco_acco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 21; calculation C05

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Tariffs and currency are material to credit quality. The temporary tariffs were overturned in February 2026, USD 21.3 million of refunds was received in the third quarter and about USD 5.0 million more in October 2026, but new tariffs took effect on 2026-07-24, so the benefit is a one-off recovery on top of a renewed cost. Currency helped nine-month sales by USD 27.6 million in 2026, yet a stronger U.S. dollar raises the cost of dollar-sourced goods sold in local currency and the issuer says it cannot always raise prices fast enough; floating-rate debt is also repricing, with the secured facilities at a weighted 5.49% against 4.66% at 2025-12-31.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_acco_acco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-K_2025-12-31_acco_acco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 45; 10-Q_2026-09-30_acco_acco-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 27–28; 10-Q_2026-09-30_acco_acco-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 30–31; 10-Q_2026-09-30_acco_acco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 35; calculation C05

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths are liquidity of USD 428.4 million with no final maturity before March 2029, a realized cost programme of USD 90.0 million, capital expenditure of 1.17% of net sales and a fixed 4.25% coupon on 65.25% of principal. Weaknesses are volume loss on a fixed cost base, derived net leverage of 4.49x (4.88x pro forma for the Trust acquisition) with a covenant definition that cannot be reproduced, customer concentration of 31.79% and the concentration of 99.17% of principal in 2029.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_acco_acco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-Q_2026-09-30_acco_acco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 34; 10-Q_2026-09-30_acco_acco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 36; 10-K_2025-12-31_acco_acco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 63; 10-K_2025-12-31_acco_acco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 106; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C01; calculation C05; calculation C14

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Opportunities that could improve credit quality are the remaining cost savings, a recovery of technology peripherals demand on the EPOS and Trust platforms, and covenant relief from deleveraging. Threats that could weaken it are further volume loss, the covenant maximum stepping down to 4.00x in the second half of 2027, the 2028 refinancing of the notes and a debt-funded acquisition.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_acco_acco-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 8–9; 10-Q_2026-09-30_acco_acco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 35; 10-Q_2026-09-30_acco_acco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 36; calculation C15

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Liquidity and the maturity profile give the issuer time. Liquidity is USD 428.4 million, the mid-year trough was USD 311.2 million and no final maturity falls before March 2029, so debt service does not depend on new market access for about two years.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_acco_acco-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 32; 10-Q_2026-09-30_acco_acco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 34; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C01

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The cost programme and low capital needs protect cash. About USD 90.0 million of savings is realized and capital expenditure is 1.17% of net sales, which keeps free cash flow positive when sales fall.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No sponsor and a capped payout limit leakage. Payouts were 82.9% of FY2025 free cash flow and the 2026 cap is USD 40.0 million, so cash is more likely to stay in the company than in a sponsor-owned peer.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_acco_acco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 63; 10-K_2025-12-31_acco_acco-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 75–76; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C05

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The fixed 4.25% coupon holds interest cost down until 2029. It applies to 65.25% of principal, so cash interest of USD 43.2 million is covered 3.63x despite lower earnings.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_acco_acco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-Q_2026-09-30_acco_acco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 35; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C14

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Earnings fall faster than sales. Derived EBITDA fell 17.98% on a net sales fall of 8.49%, and without USD 15.1 million of net tariff refunds third-quarter operating income was USD 15.2 million against USD 26.0 million, so deleveraging through earnings is not in evidence.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_acco_acco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 41; 10-K_2025-12-31_acco_acco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 62; 10-Q_2026-09-30_acco_acco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 29; calculation C06; calculation C11

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Leverage is high and its covenant measure cannot be reproduced. Derived net debt is 4.49x EBITDA and 4.88x pro forma for the Trust acquisition, against a reported ratio of 3.60x, and the maximum steps down to 4.00x in the second half of 2027.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_acco_acco-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 10–11; 10-Q_2026-09-30_acco_acco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 34; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C02; calculation C15

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Almost all debt is due in 2029. 99.17% of principal falls due in 2029 and the notes must be refinanced by September 2028, when a coupon at the 5.49% secured rate would lower derived cover to 3.11x.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_acco_acco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-Q_2026-09-30_acco_acco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_acco_acco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 35; calculation C13; calculation C14

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Customers and competition limit pricing. The five largest customers are 31.79% of net sales with 32.53% of receivables, and price offset only 18.89% of volume loss.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_acco_acco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-K_2025-12-31_acco_acco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 62; 10-K_2025-12-31_acco_acco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 106; 10-Q_2026-09-30_acco_acco-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 33–34; calculation C05; calculation C09

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: On the business side, scale is average: net sales of USD 1,524.7 million are mid-sized and have been shrinking, and a top-12 brand set supplies most of them. Competitive advantage is average, since brand rankings are management statements and private label and low entry barriers erode them. Diversification is average: two regions and 57.5% of sales outside the United States are offset by 31.79% of sales in five customers and by licence dependence in gaming accessories.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_acco_acco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-K_2025-12-31_acco_acco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-K_2025-12-31_acco_acco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-K_2025-12-31_acco_acco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 106; calculation C04; calculation C05

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: On the financial side, cost and capex flexibility is average, helped by capital expenditure of 1.17% of net sales and USD 90.0 million of realized savings but limited by the fixed cost base. Margin stability is weak, because the derived EBITDA margin fell from 12.08% in FY2024 to 9.99% over the last twelve months and the 2026 gross margin is supported by refunds. Free cash flow stability is average at best, with conversion between 30.77% and 72.75% of EBITDA. Liquidity is average to good at USD 428.4 million with a seasonal trough of USD 311.2 million, and the ability to refinance cannot be fully assessed because no rating or price is supplied. Financial policy and governance are average: no sponsor, payouts below free cash flow and a cap in 2026, offset by an amendment needed in 2025.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_acco_acco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 63; 10-Q_2026-09-30_acco_acco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 34; 10-Q_2026-09-30_acco_acco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 36; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C01; calculation C07; calculation C08

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The main supports are liquidity, the absence of maturities before March 2029, a low coupon and cost savings; the main constraints are earnings sensitivity, leverage of 5.60x on total debt and 4.49x on net debt, with 4.88x pro forma for the Trust acquisition of 2026-10-01 and 4.46x pro forma for the October 2026 tariff refunds, and the 2028 refinancing. The trend is mixed: total debt rose from USD 836.8 million at 2025-12-31 to USD 878.1 million at 2026-09-30 while derived EBITDA fell from USD 165.1 million to USD 156.7 million over the last twelve months, but seasonal cash lowered net debt. Missing for a firmer view are covenant EBITDA, the funding and earnings of Trust, ratings and market pricing.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_acco_acco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_acco_acco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 34; calculation C01; calculation C02; calculation C03; calculation C04

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over the next year or two the supports are the remaining USD 10.0 million of cost savings, USD 5.0 million of further tariff refunds received in October 2026 and the seasonal second-half cash inflow, which together should keep liquidity near the current level. The pressures are comparable sales still falling, new tariffs from 2026-07-24, restructuring cash of USD 14.8 million due within twelve months, and a covenant maximum that steps down to 4.00x in the second half of 2027; the reported ratio of 3.60x leaves a 0.40x gap to that level if nothing changes. The Trust acquisition adds technology peripherals revenue but its funding is not stated, so it is as likely to add leverage as earnings in 2027.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_acco_acco-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 8–10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_acco_acco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-Q_2026-09-30_acco_acco-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 27–28; 10-Q_2026-09-30_acco_acco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 36; calculation C03; calculation C15

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over the medium term the question is whether technology peripherals can replace declining paper-based categories before the debt falls due: the notes must be refinanced by September 2028 and 99.17% of principal is due in 2029. Sector headwinds are structural digital substitution, private label and tariff policy; tailwinds are limited to the school season and recovery in learning and creative categories, which the issuer says has not offset technology peripherals declines. Company tailwinds are low capital needs and a fixed low coupon; company headwinds are concentration and a fixed cost base.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_acco_acco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-Q_2026-09-30_acco_acco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_acco_acco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 33; calculation C14

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The realistic downside starts with another year of broad volume decline of the FY2025 kind, with tariff refunds ending and the new tariffs applying to a base in which a majority of products are sourced from Asia. The first operational break is gross margin: without refunds the nine-month 2026 margin was already 31.31% against 32.48%, and fixed costs of selling, general and administrative expenses and amortization do not fall with volume. Financial transmission follows the FY2025 pattern, where EBITDA fell 17.98% on a sales fall of 8.49%; if EBITDA fell by the same proportion from USD 156.7 million to USD 128.52 million, derived net debt on the unchanged USD 703.4 million would be 5.47x EBITDA (the pro forma Trust position would be higher). This is an illustration of scale and not a forecast.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_acco_acco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 41; 10-K_2025-12-31_acco_acco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 62; 10-Q_2026-09-30_acco_acco-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 30–31; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C06; calculation C10; calculation C19

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity would absorb the shock for several quarters: the revolver availability of USD 253.7 million and cash of USD 174.7 million compare with a seasonal swing of USD 117.2 million between the 2026 mid-year trough and the third quarter. The consequences land on leverage and refinancing rather than liquidity: the reported covenant ratio has 0.40x to the 4.00x maximum from the second half of 2027, the size of the cushion in EBITDA cannot be calculated, and a weaker earnings base would make the 2028 refinancing of the USD 575.0 million notes costlier than the USD 7.13 million a year illustrated at the secured rate. Management levers are the remaining USD 10.0 million of savings, USD 27.0 million of annual dividends, the 2026 payout cap, the low capital expenditure and asset sales, which produced USD 18.7 million of proceeds in 2025. Resilience looks sufficient to avoid liquidity distress through 2027 and not sufficient to avoid pressure on the covenant and on refinancing terms. The observable triggers are comparable sales, the reported covenant ratio each quarter and revolver borrowings after the second-half inflow.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_acco_acco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 47; 10-Q_2026-09-30_acco_acco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_acco_acco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 34; 10-Q_2026-09-30_acco_acco-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 35; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C01; calculation C13; calculation C15; calculation C17

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, ACCO presents an adequate business profile supported by established brand positions, low capital needs and a largely realized cost programme, but credit quality is constrained by volume loss on a fixed cost base, customer concentration and derived net leverage of 4.49x, or 4.88x pro forma for the Trust acquisition of 2026-10-01. Cash-flow durability appears adequate rather than steady: free cash flow has been positive every year but ranged between 30.77% and 72.75% of EBITDA. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on stabilised comparable sales, the covenant ratio and market pricing for a USD 575.0 million refinancing due by September 2028. The primary downside path is volume loss on a fixed cost base ahead of that refinancing. Further analysis would require covenant EBITDA and definitions, the funding and earnings of Trust, and ratings and market pricing. Fundamental credit review completed. Top risk: earnings sensitivity to volume ahead of the 2028 refinancing.

fields.value: - Medium: No agency rating, bond price or loan price is supplied, so refinancing access and the cost of replacing the 4.25% notes cannot be assessed beyond the 5.49% secured-facility reference; ratings and market pricing would close it.
